results.name: desktop-pixels
notes: One opaque coordinate-encoded pattern per monitor; compares every monitor pixel after full virtual-desktop capture. Unoccupied gaps between monitors are excluded. No mouse/keyboard injection, and no desktop-content screenshots are saved.
100 repeated 320x240-or-smaller window/capture/destruction cycles check RGB and GDI/USER resource counts. Other DPI/layout combinations require rerunning after changing display settings.

results.name: capture
notes: Timing includes BitBlt, GdiFlush, and copying into reusable opaque BGRA Bitmap storage; it excludes UI overlay display.
Full-desktop benchmark uses CAPTUREBLT. Region results compare SRCCOPY and SRCCOPY|CAPTUREBLT; no desktop pixels are saved.
The pass flag checks desktop capture p95 <= 150 ms and an available 1920x1080 monitor region; desktop pixel accuracy is tested separately by the E2E pattern test.
1080p CAPTUREBLT p95 exceeds 15 ms: evaluate DXGI capture on Windows 8+ in P5; retain BitBlt fallback for Windows 7.

results.name: overlay
notes: Actual virtual-desktop window; first half moves a 640x360 selection, second half moves a selection spanning 75% of each canvas dimension. Symmetric-difference strips, borders and labels are redrawn.
Timers include synchronous WM_PAINT and GdiFlush; exclude DWM presentation/vsync. Frozen desktop pixels are never written to disk.
This machine's canvas differs from AC0-5's 7680x2160 target; this run is not evidence for that exact configuration.

results.name: pin
notes: 320x240 layered window with opaque center, premultiplied-alpha border and transparent margin. Capture compares opaque RGB exactly; blended RGB allows one channel level of compositor rounding.
100 create/present/destroy cycles. Pixel checks run at 100% and 80% global opacity on the first and last cycles. This prototype does not implement P4 pin interactions.

results.name: gif
notes: Real desktop BitBlt capture of a controlled 1280x720 animated pattern; SRCCOPY without CAPTUREBLT, full opaque GIF frames, 30/30/40 ms delay cycle.
Every captured frame matches the displayed source pattern; every decoded WIC frame is checked against its captured RGB hash. WIC validates decoding, not browser/Photos playback.

Harness costs are reported separately: pattern generation/painting, GdiFlush+DwmFlush presentation wait, RGB verification, and file writes. The drop count measures this complete sequential experiment, not a production recorder. Use capture_plus_encode plus the independent capture spike to assess the acquisition bottleneck.

P0 uses one UI/capture/encode thread and one pending compressed frame. P5 still needs parallel encoding, changed rectangles, transparency, cursor capture, backpressure, lock-screen pause, and preview UI. Wu fallback is unit-tested; this <=8-color workload exercises exact palettes.
AC0-6 no-drop target is not met by the sequential prototype. Use these timings to budget P5 worker parallelism; preserved GIF duration does not hide dropped ticks.
